summary: How to get ready for davening: think seriously first, and once you start, don't stop for anything.

chunks.en: We only stand up to daven
chunks.st: One may only stand and begin to pray

chunks.en: with a serious, humble feeling.
chunks.st: from an approach of gravity and submission.

words.note: A heavy head means a serious, humble mood.

chunks.he: חֲסִידִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים הָיוּ שׁוֹהִים שָׁעָה אַחַת
chunks.en: The pious people of long ago would wait one hour
chunks.st: There is a tradition that the early generations of pious men would wait one hour,
chunks.stMore: in order to reach the solemn frame of mind appropriate for prayer,

words.note: Very holy people who did more than they had to.

chunks.he: וּמִתְפַּלְּלִים, כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּכַוְּנוּ אֶת לִבָּם לַמָּקוֹם.
chunks.en: and then daven, so they could turn their hearts to Hashem.
chunks.st: and then pray, so that they would focus their hearts toward their Father in Heaven.
chunks.stMore: Standing in prayer is standing before God and, as such,

words.note: "HaMakom" is a name for Hashem, Who is everywhere.

chunks.en: Even if the king says hello to him,
chunks.st: even if the king greets him,

chunks.en: he should not answer him.
chunks.st: he should not respond to him;

chunks.en: And even if a snake is wrapped around his heel,
chunks.st: and even if a snake is wrapped on his heel,

chunks.en: he should not stop davening.
chunks.st: he should not interrupt his prayer.

summary: Where in Shemoneh Esrei we add words about rain and the Havdalah prayer on Motzei Shabbos.
stIntro: This mishna speaks of additions to the standard formula of the Amida prayer and the blessings in which they are incorporated.

chunks.en: We mention Hashem's power of rain in the bracha about bringing the dead back to life,
chunks.explain: This means saying Mashiv haruach umorid hageshem.
chunks.st: One mentions the might of the rains and recites: He makes the wind blow and the rain fall, in the second blessing of the Amida prayer, the blessing of the revival of the dead.

words.note: The second bracha of Shemoneh Esrei, "Mechayei Hameisim."

chunks.en: and we ask for rain in the bracha for the years,
chunks.explain: This means saying Vesein tal umatar.
chunks.st: And the request for rain: And grant dew and rain as a blessing, in the ninth blessing of the Amida prayer, the blessing of the years.

words.note: The bracha "Bareich Aleinu," asking for good crops.

chunks.en: and Havdalah goes in the bracha "Who grants knowledge" (Atah Chonen).
chunks.explain: On Motzei Shabbos we add Atah Chonantanu there.
chunks.st: And the prayer of distinction [havdala], between the holy and the profane recited in the evening prayer following Shabbat and festivals, in the fourth blessing of the Amida prayer: Who graciously grants knowledge.

words.note: Words that separate Shabbos or Yom Tov from the weekday.
The bracha "Atah Chonen," asking for wisdom.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: it is said as a fourth bracha all by itself.
chunks.st: Havdala is recited as an independent fourth blessing.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says, it goes in Modim, the thank-you bracha.
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says that it is recited in the seventeenth blessing of the Amida prayer, the blessing of thanksgiving.

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.
The bracha "Modim," where we thank Hashem.

summary: Some wrong things a chazzan might say, and what to do if the chazzan makes a mistake.
stIntro: Concluding the laws of prayer in this tractate, the mishna raises several prayer-related matters. This mishna speaks of certain innovations in the prayer formula that warrant the silencing of a communal prayer leader who attempts to introduce them in his prayers, as their content tends toward heresy.

chunks.he: הָאוֹמֵר עַל קַן צִפּוֹר יַגִּיעוּ רַחֲמֶיךָ,
chunks.en: Someone who says, "Your mercy reaches even a bird's nest,"
chunks.st: One who recites in his supplication: Just as Your mercy is extended to a bird’s nest,
chunks.stMore: as You have commanded us to send away the mother before taking her chicks or eggs (Deuteronomy 22:6–7), so too extend Your mercy to us;

words.note: The mitzvah to send away a mother bird before taking the eggs.

chunks.en: or "May Your Name be mentioned for the good,"
chunks.st: and one who recites: May Your name be mentioned with the good

chunks.en: or "Modim, Modim," saying "we thank" twice,
chunks.st: or one who recites: We give thanks, we give thanks twice,

chunks.en: we make him stop.
chunks.explain: These words can give a wrong idea about Hashem.
chunks.st: they silence him.
chunks.stMore: This mishna and the next one deal with the communal prayer leader. (If one says: “May the good bless You,” this is a path of heresy.)

chunks.en: If the chazzan leading the davening makes a mistake,
chunks.st: One who is passing before the ark, as prayer leader, and erred,

words.note: The aron where the Sefer Torah is; the chazzan stands in front of it.

chunks.en: someone else should take his place right away,
chunks.st: another should immediately pass in his place,

chunks.en: and at that time he should not say "no thanks" to be polite.
chunks.explain: Usually, people politely say no when first asked to lead.
chunks.st: and at that moment, this replacement should not refuse in the interest of courtesy.
chunks.stMore: The Amida prayer was interrupted and he should replace him as quickly as possible.

chunks.en: Where does the new chazzan start?
chunks.st: From where does the replacement commence?

chunks.en: From the beginning of the bracha where the mistake was.
chunks.st: From the beginning of the blessing in which the former had erred.

summary: The chazzan should be careful not to get mixed up, so he doesn't answer Amen to the Kohanim or do Birkas Kohanim himself.
stIntro: In order to prevent the prayer leader from erring in his prayer, it was said that

chunks.en: The chazzan leading the davening
chunks.st: one who passes before the ark

words.note: The aron where the Sefer Torah is; the chazzan stands in front of it.

chunks.en: should not answer Amen after the Kohanim's bracha,
chunks.st: should not respond amen after the blessing of the priests,

words.note: Kohanim bless the people with Birkas Kohanim.

chunks.en: because he might get mixed up.
chunks.st: because of potential confusion.
chunks.stMore: Since the mishna is describing a situation in which he was praying without a prayer book, responding amen would interrupt the order of the prayer and potentially lead him to begin a different blessing.

chunks.he: וְאִם אֵין שָׁם כֹּהֵן אֶלָּא הוּא,
chunks.en: And even if the chazzan is the only Kohen there,
chunks.st: For this reason, even if there is no priest other than the communal prayer leader,

chunks.en: he should not raise his hands to bless the people.
chunks.st: he does not lift his hands to bless the people, lest he become confused.

chunks.en: But if he is sure
chunks.st: And, however, if he is certain

chunks.en: that he can raise his hands to bless
chunks.st: that he can lift his hands

chunks.en: and go back to his davening, he may do it.
chunks.st: and resume his prayer without becoming confused, he is permitted to recite the blessing.

summary: A mistake in davening is a bad sign. Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa could tell if his prayers for sick people were accepted.
stIntro: Concluding its discussion of the halakhot of prayer, the mishna discusses less practical aspects of prayer.

chunks.en: If someone davens and makes a mistake,
chunks.st: One who prays and realizes that he erred in his prayer,

chunks.en: it is a bad sign for him.
chunks.explain: It shows his tefillah was not accepted.
chunks.st: it is a bad omen for him;
chunks.stMore: it indicates to him that his prayer was not accepted.

chunks.en: And if he is the chazzan,
chunks.st: And if he who erred is the communal prayer leader,

words.note: The chazzan, who davens for everyone.

chunks.en: it is a bad sign for the people who sent him,
chunks.st: it is a bad omen for those who sent him,

chunks.en: because a person's messenger is like the person himself.
chunks.st: because a person’s agent has legal status equivalent to his own.

chunks.en: They said about
chunks.st: On a similar note, they said about

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa,
chunks.st: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah, famous for his holy prayers.

chunks.en: that when he davened for sick people, he would say,
chunks.st: that he would pray on behalf of the sick and immediately after his prayer he would say:

chunks.en: "This one will live, and this one will die."
chunks.st: This one shall recover from his illness and live and this one shall die.

chunks.en: They asked him,
chunks.st: When they said to him:

chunks.en: "How do you know?"
chunks.st: From where do you know?

chunks.en: He told them,
chunks.st: He said to them:

chunks.en: "If my tefillah flows smoothly from my mouth,
chunks.st: If my prayer is fluent in my mouth as I recite it and there are no errors,

chunks.en: I know that it was accepted.
chunks.st: I know that my prayer is accepted.

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: And if not,

chunks.en: I know that it was not accepted."
chunks.st: I know that my prayer is rejected.
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura's first explanation: the sick person is "torn away" and will not live.
